newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter to buy online Lombard Brokerage.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter to buy online Lombard Brokerage.

text.p: Dean Witter Discover & Co. said Monday it agreed to acquire online stock brokers Lombard Brokerage Inc., a San Francisco-based company that offers securities transactions via the Internet.

The company said Lombard, founded in 1992, has won awards for its Website and recently was named "the best online broker" by Barron's. Lombard conducts business in all 50 states and the District of Columbia.
Both Dean Witter and Lombard declined to disclose terms of the transaction.
Eric Roach, Lombard's founder, will remain with the company as chairman and chief executive officer.
A spokesman for Dean Witter said Lombard would be "totally separate and distinct" from Dean Witter's other main business.
Dean Witter has 9,000 stockbrokers, ranking the firm third in the United States behind Merrill Lynch and Co. Inc. and Smith Barney & Co., a unit of Travelers Group Inc.
"This gives us access to new market segments, electronic delivery, electronic distribution," said Dean Witter spokesman Timothy Lee.

Under the most recent pricing schedule announced by Lombard, customers willing to trade electronically were being charged $14.95 to trade up to 5,000 shares for exchange-listed stocks and for Nasdaq issues.

Lombard was charging $19.95 for limit orders to buy or sell up to 5,000 shares of listed and Nasdaq stocks. Limit orders allow the customer to specify a price at which he is willing to sell or buy stock and the order is executed if the market price reaches the customer's price.
Lombard was founded as a deep discount broker in 1992 by Roach, the firm's president and chief executive. The firm started online trading on the Internet in August, 1995.
Lombard has said it is adding new users to its service at the rate of 600 a day. Lombard 45,000 accounts compared with 3 million at Dean Witter, a Dean Witter spokesman said.
A news release issued in August said Lombard had revenue of $24 million in 1995. The firm said online trading over the Internet accounted for 20 percent of its revenue and trades.
Other big players in electronic broking include Charles Schwab Corp., E*Trade and PC Financial Network, a unit of Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
